column1: # Phrasing that reads as a word-for-word translation from Japanese. scripts/suspects.py reads this file.
# pattern: a Python regular expression, matched without regard to case against each sentence, after
#          inline code, link targets, and URLs are taken out. ^ is the start of the sentence.
# example: a sentence the pattern points at. The plugin's test runs the script on every example.
# instead: what to write in its place.

column2: example
column3: instead

column2: It is necessary to restart the server after the update.
column3: use "need to", "must", or the verb alone: "Restart the server after the update."

column2: We changed the setting in order to reduce the load.
column3: use "to": "We changed the setting to reduce the load."

column1: ^(?:regarding|concerning|as for|with regard to|in regard to|with respect to)\b[^,]*,
column2: Regarding the login error, we fixed it yesterday.
column3: start with the subject: "We fixed the login error yesterday."

column2: Please perform the confirmation of the settings.
column3: use the verb inside the noun: "Please confirm the settings."

column2: We will make a confirmation with the team tomorrow.
column3: use the verb: "We will confirm with the team tomorrow."

column2: It is possible to change the port in the settings.
column3: use "can" with a subject: "You can change the port in the settings."

column2: After the update, it becomes possible to export the report.
column3: use "can" with a subject: "After the update, you can export the report."

column2: There is a possibility that the nightly job fails.
column3: use "may" or "might": "The nightly job may fail."

column2: It can be said that the new design is faster.
column3: state the claim, or name who holds it: "The new design is faster."

column2: In the case of an error, the tool stops.
column3: use "if" or "when": "If an error occurs, the tool stops."

column2: We fixed two bugs in this time.
column3: use "this time", or name the release: "We fixed two bugs in this release."

column2: Please note that the tool deletes the cache every night.
column3: state the fact: "The tool deletes the cache every night."

column2: The usage method is in the README.
column3: use "how to" and a verb: "The README shows how to use it."

column2: The tool reads formats such as JSON, YAML, etc.
column3: keep "such as" or "etc.", not both: "The tool reads formats such as JSON and YAML."

column2: The server handles authentication information management.
column3: unstack the nouns with a verb: "The server manages the sign-in details."

column2: We will correspond to the issue next week.
column3: name the action: "We will fix the issue next week."

column2: From the viewpoint of security, we keep the keys offline.
column3: use "for": "For security, we keep the keys offline."

column2: We added the flag with the aim of saving time.
column3: use "to": "We added the flag to save time."

column2: The above-mentioned settings apply to every user.
column3: use "these", or name the thing: "These settings apply to every user."

column2: Run the command as below.
column3: end the sentence and put the command after it: "Run this command."

column2: Can use the command on Linux too.
column3: add the subject: "You can use the command on Linux too."

column2: Confirmed that the build passes on Linux.
column3: add the subject: "We confirmed that the build passes on Linux."
